title: LiveWorld — A design brief the world can check
disclosures: Actual application screenshots and native 30 fps simulation replay exports
Explicitly labelled diagrams derived from recomputed engine evidence; not application screenshots
One previously observed AI-generated tabletop input and its recorded rescan
Recorded Meta contract translation and playtest, independently recomputed
Authored showcase, not a held-out benchmark or physical-camera test
Inference waiting time omitted; generic synthetic English narration

scenes.heading: The same total can hide a very different game.
scenes.caption: Same synthetic world · minimum on-time deliveries per home: 0 → 3 · four units remain late
scenes.narration: Twenty deliveries on time in both worlds. But one leaves a home with none. The other gives every home at least three. LiveWorld helps game creators test the difference.

scenes.heading: One table becomes one playable experiment.
scenes.caption: AI-generated input · saved Muse Spark + SAM capture · confirmed roles on a fixed grid
scenes.narration: A cup becomes the well, blocks become homes, and sticks become bridges. This input is generated. Recorded Muse Spark and SAM outputs supplied the objects and shapes. Confirmed roles and image-relative positions become a fixed-grid world, not a metric reconstruction.

scenes.heading: Say what a good design should do.
scenes.caption: Recorded Meta translation · at least 20 total, at least 3 per home, at most 10 waiting turns
scenes.narration: The creator asks for at least twenty on-time units, at least three at every home, and at most ten waiting turns. Muse Spark translates this into a contract. The creator confirms it. Each repair keeps workers, demand, deadlines and production locked.

scenes.heading: A shorter queue can hide a losing household.
scenes.caption: Recorded rescan + engine evidence diagram · waiting 22 → 10 · total stays 20/24 · per-home floor FAILS
scenes.narration: Moving the lower stick looks promising: waiting falls from twenty-two to ten turns. Yet the total stays twenty of twenty-four. The household comparison reveals the problem. Four late units move from one home to another. This proposal fails the confirmed per-home floor.

scenes.heading: Every explanation has a receipt.
scenes.caption: Engine events + replay frames · dispatch, arrival, bridge visits and outbound waiting
scenes.narration: Inspect a home and its delivery receipts. Each receipt records dispatch, arrival, bridge visits and waiting, with references to the simulator's events. Select an arrival to replay the exact turn and highlight its courier. Across worlds, deliveries are matched by home and order, not assumed to be the same parcel.

scenes.heading: A fairer design, verified against the brief.
scenes.caption: Recorded Meta playtest · balanced dispatch · 20/24 on time · wait 7 · every home ≥3
scenes.narration: The recorded Meta playtester tests a dispatch change and uses a systematic simulator search. Balanced dispatch meets every condition: twenty units on time, waiting seven turns, and at least three on time at every home. Four units still arrive late. Three previously fully served homes each give up one on-time unit.

scenes.heading: Find where the design stops working.
scenes.caption: Lower bridge shifted equally in A and B · −1 cell breaks wait cap; +1 breaks on-time floor
scenes.narration: Now shift the lower bridge one cell in either direction in both worlds. The nominal balanced design passes. One direction breaks its waiting cap; the other breaks its on-time target. These are selected deterministic conditions, not a statistical reliability score. No model calls are needed for the sweep.

scenes.heading: Keep the design, the brief and the evidence.
scenes.caption: Actual save and reopen · contract, trials and checkpoints retained · imported results recomputed
scenes.narration: Save the project, open it again, and recompute every trial. The contract and checkpoints travel with the world. Export household tradeoffs, delivery receipts and sensitivity conditions, or a replay with its inputs. Imported success claims are discarded. Eight predeclared interpretation checks matched the expected contracts or refusals, one attempt each. This small integration check is not a general accuracy benchmark.

scenes.heading: Build a world. State the goal. Test the tradeoff.
scenes.caption: Tang Vu · Meta interprets; the engine verifies · local generated-input prototype
scenes.narration: LiveWorld was built by Tang Vu for indie creators. Meta interprets the scene and design intent, and orchestrates experiments. The simulator verifies outcomes. Three.js renders the world. This is a generated-input local prototype. Physical capture and creator usability still need broader validation.
